newsitem.title: UK: Freight demand steady for Cuban sugar to Black Sea.
newsitem.headline: Freight demand steady for Cuban sugar to Black Sea.

text.p: Cuban bulk sugar destined for the Black Sea was the only item of new business on the sugar freight market on Wednesday as the island's 1996/97 shipment cycle got under way in earnest, shipbrokers said.
Pacol quoted two new Cuba orders, both to the Black Sea, seeking tonnage to cover 14,000 tonnes for 18/25 January and for 25,000 tonnes for early February.
Gill & Duffus was also in the market to cover a Cuba order for 14,000 tonnes to Egypt or the Black Sea for prompt dates.

Polish charterers Gdynia Amerika quoted for 20/22,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to the Black Sea for mid-January onwards. Shipbrokers cited a handful of fixtures from various origins but details of rates achieved have yet to emerge.

CSR fixed 30,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Crockett for mid-January and Mauritius Sugar Syndicate (MSS) covered its earlier order for 15,000 tonnes, again in bulk, from Port Louis to London or Greenock for the end of January.
Market sources said the MSS fixture rate was likely to be close to stg 14.25, which was the rate reported for the last similar fixture.

E D & F Man fixed 6,000 tonnes of preslung bagged sugar from Santander to Syria for prompt shipment dates and Genoc fixed a prompt 13/14,000-tonne bagged cargo from south Brazil to Mediterranean, Red Sea, Umm Qasr, Pakistan or Colombo. --Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
